title: An ideal lies in the Jacobson radical iff 1 + I consists of units
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with Jacobson radical $\operatorname{rad}(R)$ (the intersection of all maximal ideals of $R$) and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal. Then $I\subseteq\operatorname{rad}(R)$ if and only if every element of $1+I=\{1+x:x\in I\}$ is a unit of $R$.

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line per direction: `Ideal.mem_jacobson_bot : x ∈ jacobson (⊥ : Ideal R) ↔ ∀ y, IsUnit (x * y + 1)` (line 288; `jacobson ⊥` is the intersection of the maximal ideals, i.e. rad(R)). (⇒) for x ∈ I ≤ jacobson ⊥ take y = 1: IsUnit (x * 1 + 1) = IsUnit (1 + x). (⇐) for x ∈ I and any y, x * y ∈ I, so 1 + x * y is a unit, i.e. IsUnit (x * y + 1) by add_comm; hence x ∈ jacobson ⊥.
